audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Undying Rage as Fury-gated in four places — 'before his Fury fills R', 'if his Fury is up, Undying Rage survives it', 'Stack Fury so Undying Rage (R) is up' — and credits his healing to Fury itself. Mocking Shout is never mentioned, and the clone is again called 'clone and invis'.
audit.why: Riot's kit: R Undying Rage costs 0 and runs on 120/100/80s — Fury is not a requirement, so 'burst him before his Fury fills' is advice that will get the player killed. Fury raises crit chance; the healing is Bloodlust (Q), 12s, which consumes Fury to heal. W Mocking Shout, 850 range and 14s, cuts AD and slows enemies with their backs turned — the reason disengaging fails. E Spinning Slash is 650 range on 12/11/10/9/8s. Neeko's W has no invisibility.
audit.corrected: R stated as a flat cooldown with no Fury cost, healing attributed to Bloodlust with a Grievous Wounds call, Mocking Shout named as the escape-denial, and E given its range and cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Neeko level 1 and level 6 while its own whys[0] describes him spinning on her at every last-hit and whys[4] says Undying Rage survives the combo.
audit.why: Packet chart is Tryndamere on every row except level 6 (Skill), on a 30% win rate, and matches the existing prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 and 4 set to Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Skill in both layers with matching ratings and whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike framed the kill window as a race against his Fury bar.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is 120/105/90 against Undying Rage at 120/100/80 — the real spike question is whether his R is on cooldown, not how full his Fury is.
audit.corrected: Spike now names the flat R cooldown as the thing to track.

edits.before: Do not try to lane this straight up. The second you step into your Q-poke range to last-hit, Tryndamere spins (E) on top of you and his Fury-healed crit autos out-trade your single Q tick instantly. At Levels 1-3 you have no combo and no escape if his E is up, so hold W (Shapesplitter) to dodge his gap-close rather than to chase. Farm with the far edge of Q, concede CS you cannot safely take, and remember his autos heal more than your poke chunks.
edits.after: Do not lane this straight up. The second you step into Q range to last-hit, Spinning Slash covers 650 and his crit autos out-trade your single Q tick while Bloodlust heals it back — buy Grievous Wounds early. At Levels 1-3 you have no combo and no escape with his E up, so keep Shapesplitter (W) to bait the gap-close, not to chase, and remember Mocking Shout slows you the moment your back is turned. Farm the far edge of Q and concede CS you cannot take.

edits.before: Level 6 is the one window where you can theoretically win the duel: a max-range E (Tangle-Barbs) root into Q and a Pop Blossom stun can burst a low-Fury Tryndamere. But the catch defines this lane — if his Fury bar is up, he simply presses Undying Rage (R) mid-combo and lives at 1 HP for 5 seconds, then spins out and kills you while your shields drop. Only commit when you have hard proof his R is on cooldown, otherwise you are feeding. Far better to use your clone and disguise to leave lane and gank a real target.
edits.after: Level 6 is the one window where you can theoretically win the duel: a max-range E (Tangle-Barbs) root into Q and a Pop Blossom stun can burst him outright. But the catch defines this lane — Undying Rage costs nothing and needs no Fury, it just runs on 120/100/80s, so he presses it mid-combo, lives at 1 HP, then spins out and kills you. Only commit with hard proof that his R is on cooldown, otherwise you are feeding. Better still, use the clone and disguise to leave lane and gank a real target.

notes: The Fury-gated ult was the most dangerous error in my slice: the page told the player to burst him 'before his Fury fills R', which invites a commit into a fully available 120s ultimate. Undying Rage has no Fury requirement and no cost.
